data.narrative:
Carbon Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $177M to date, is evaluated against a comp universe of one public company and eight private peers in the same sector. The peer set includes three directly comparable Series C stage companies: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $177M total raised proxy, yielding $301M. The peer-median method uses the three same-sector, same-stage comparables, which exhibit a median valuation of $1.0B (range: $1.0B–$1.6B). These methods produce materially different signals, reflecting the gap between capital-deployed benchmarking and market-traded peer valuations.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $256M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $650M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around whether Carbon Robotics tracks closer to its capital-raise profile or commands peer-set multiples. Key uncertainties include unit economics relative to the peer cohort, revenue scale and growth trajectory, and whether the company's technology differentiation justifies positioning toward the upper range. Additional diligence on revenue, retention, and gross margins relative to Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics would refine this range materially.
